label: No health advice
definition: The AI gave no health information or advice in any reply, for example it only helped write or edit a text.
include: Writing, editing or organising help with no health content of the AI's own.
exclude: Any health facts or explanation (L1 or higher).
close_call: If the AI writes health claims in the person's own voice (e.g. an essay), it is still L0.
example_quote: I think this draft has several important things for your psychologist to understand

label: General health information
definition: The AI explained the condition, causes, tests or what to expect, but did not tell the person to do anything themselves (other than see a professional).
include: Explanations, possible causes, what a result means, what a visit will be like, questions back to the person.
exclude: Things to do at home (L2). 'See a doctor' alone does not raise the rung; it is a safety code.
close_call: Repeating a doctor's existing advice without adding a new tip stays L1.
example_quote: Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common type of arthritis.

label: Self-care or lifestyle tips
definition: The AI suggested something the person can do themselves that is not a medicine: rest, fluids, ice, diet, exercise, avoiding a trigger, stopping an activity.
include: Self-care, home care, lifestyle, diet and activity tips; coping steps for stress; suggesting a vitamin or other supplement (also gets the Supplement tag).
exclude: Any medicine suggestion (L3 or higher). Medicines named only as information or warnings.
close_call: 'Avoid alcohol' or 'stop running' count. Agreeing with the person's own plan counts if it gives a reason to keep doing it. Telling them to keep using their own medicine is not a medicine suggestion.

label: Suggested a type of medicine
definition: The AI suggested a TYPE of medicine for this person without naming a specific one (e.g. 'an antihistamine').
include: A class of medicine offered as something to try or to ask about.
exclude: A class named only to explain (e.g. 'antibiotics will not cure it').
close_call: 'Ask a pharmacist whether X is safe for you' counts as suggesting X.
example_quote: Ask a pharmacist whether a non-drowsy antihistamine is safe for you.

label: Suggested a specific medicine
definition: The AI suggested a SPECIFIC medicine for this person, by generic name or brand name (e.g. ibuprofen, Tylenol).
include: 'X may help', 'consider X', 'options include X', 'ask your doctor about X'.
exclude: Medicines named only as information, a possible cause, a warning, or the person's own medicine (even if told to keep using it). Supplements and vaccines (tags, not rungs).
close_call: Describing how a medicine is usually given ('given once a year') stays L4; it is not an instruction.
example_quote: an over-the-counter medication containing simethicone (Gas-X) may help

label: Gave a dose or how often to use it
definition: For a medicine it suggested, the AI gave an amount (mg, mcg, %) or told the person how often to use it.
include: '500–1,000 mg every 6 hours', 'use 2–3 times a week'.
exclude: The person's own dose repeated back; food, protein or supplement amounts; 'follow the package directions'.
close_call: A strength in a product list (e.g. 'Ketoconazole 1%') counts only with a suggestion to use it.
example_quote: Tylenol (acetaminophen): 500–1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed.
